title: This Week in Finance & Tech
body:
The week ahead looks quiet for U.S. markets as futures remain flat. Investors are holding their breath for upcoming inflation data and watching the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, where new demands from Iran have dimmed hopes for a quick reopening. This uncertainty is being felt in the UK as well, with warnings that the ongoing conflict in the Middle East could impact economic growth next year by driving up fuel prices and disrupting supply chains.

In the world of AI, OpenAI is making significant moves. Free users of ChatGPT will soon have access to unlimited text chats, removing the rate limits that previously cut off conversations. However, the company is also facing legal and hardware questions. New court filings suggest OpenAI plans to challenge Apple in a trade secrets lawsuit by pointing to Apple's own loose security practices. On the hardware front, reports indicate OpenAI is developing an AI-focused device that functions like a smart speaker, expected to cost between $300 and $400.

Elsewhere in tech and policy, Google Wallet is rolling out a new feature that lets parents set up secure balances for their children, aimed at teaching financial habits with built-in oversight. Meanwhile, in the UK, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced plans to give local councils more power to restrict the number of vape and betting shops, a move intended to help revitalize town centers that have struggled with decline.

Finally, in Washington, President Donald Trump is renewing his attempt to remove Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook. This follows a previous effort that was blocked by the Supreme Court, as the administration continues to push for more allies on the central bank's board.
